patch.value: Privacy gate still classifies generic procfs documentation as an absolute host path

Tracks gh:unbraind/pm-github#193 (filed 2026-10-28, missed by the blind issue watch). The absolute-host-path rule on current main still lists proc among its sensitive roots with the same delimiter policy, so public Linux documentation like /proc/<pid> examples produces findings that block gated issue sync (originally observed importing a reviewer repo's issue #56, whose daily sync is still failing as of 2026-11-02, run 41408058207). The 2026.10.30 'privacy precision' changes (PR #198) tightened other rules but not this classification. Needed: either narrow the proc root match to concrete host-like usage (account/pid-shaped paths) or document and default to the supported content-hash allowlist for affected repositories, with a regression fixture carrying generic procfs documentation.
